title: Retaining the Talents of 'Ready Now' Leaders
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses a specific succession-planning gap: organizations tend to invest thoughtfully in developing leaders who are years away from a senior role, but neglect leaders classified as 'Ready Now,' who are fully prepared but simply waiting for a senior seat to open up. Because top jobs are scarce, this piece argues the queue of Ready Now candidates is often larger than available roles, creating real flight risk to competitors who can offer the title sooner. It surveys several structural strategies organizations use to buy time and retain these leaders, including co-head structures that double senior opportunities, extended rotational assignments in unfamiliar units or geographies, and 18-24 month developmental roles that expose Ready Now leaders to new parts of the business. It closes by insisting a succession plan without a retention strategy for its most prepared leaders isn't really a plan.
points: Organizations often invest heavily in developing leaders years from readiness but neglect fully 'Ready Now' leaders who are simply waiting for an opening.
Co-head leadership structures are cited as one growing tactic for doubling the number of senior opportunities available.
Extended rotational assignments — a year or two leading a different culture, region, or specialized unit — are used to buy time while further developing the leader.
18-24 month developmental 'number two' or special-projects roles let Ready Now leaders gain new exposure while awaiting a permanent seat.
quotes: The best organizations are highly thoughtful about the development opportunities for leaders on the runway toward a bigger role, but they often scratch their heads when it comes to Ready Now leaders waiting for a top job to open up.
Senior roles and positions are typically hard to come by in most organizations, so there are usually more Ready Now candidates sitting in the queue than is ideal.
By having units, divisions, groups, and functions led by two people, organizations double the opportunities for Ready Now leaders.
Increasingly popular is for organizations to create a developmental role for 18-24 months where Ready Now leaders can see the organization from a different vantage and get themselves set.
A succession plan without a talent retention strategy for Ready Now leaders isn’t much of a plan at all.
